story_angle: consumer report reviewing the apocalypse's amenities, with star rating
headline: Roundabout Arbitration Tents Rated Four Stars as Traffic Negotiations Trigger Nationwide Exodus
deck: Residents flee gridlock disasters while munching on 'I'm Yielding' mints and flashing courtesy cards.
article: Consumer Reports issued its 2026 Apocalypse Amenities Update, assigning roundabout arbitration tents a 4.5-star score for shaded benches and coffee refills during 14-hour yield standoffs. Yield-sign diplomacy kits scored just 2 stars after 63 percent of testers looped back into endless courtesy cycles. Commuter Bobbie Lane described circling an intersection for hours after a simple left turn. Emergency provisions now include single-serve 'I'm Yielding' mints and pocket flashcards. Harold G. Teere of Traffic Negotiation Support Services called the items essential for anyone still on the roads.
author: Clarence D. Crosswalk, Senior Intersection Analyst

oped.title: Hats Off to Gridlock: The Exodus Is Just Weak Negotiators Self-Deporting
oped.author: Sir Cedric Yieldsworth, Grand Arbiter of Monocle-Based Right-of-Way at the Roundabout Purity League
oped.body: The flight from four-star tents after brief delays is no crisis; it is overdue housecleaning. Sun hats block eye contact and courtesy-card signals at peak merge times. As owner of the sole monocle kiosk at the busiest interchange, I propose mandatory hat checks at every entrance, enforced by my new etiquette constabulary. Mint-chewing refugees will give way to serious diplomats who relish debating lane order until dusk. Progress requires complicating the obvious; anything simpler disrespects the roundabout.

classifieds.text: Selling my entire fleet of negotiation flashcards and yield signs after the latest 4-hour roundabout standoff. All proceeds going toward my one-way ticket out of this mess.
Wanted: Skilled roundabout mediator with experience in flashcard diplomacy and mint distribution. Must tolerate honking and existential traffic rage. Apply before the next exodus wave.
LOST: My will to live at the intersection of Chaos and Despair. Found: Abandoned 'I'm Yielding' mints and a stack of four-star rated arbitration tents. Claim at City Hall before residents flee.
Single professional seeking partner for the nationwide gridlock exodus. Must be proficient in courtesy card flashing and roundabout yielding etiquette. Serious inquiries only; no non-yielders.

panels.caption: Arbitration tent glowing with four stars as horns blare: "Sir, your merge priority expires in six minutes."
Bureaucrat hands out mints: "Flash the courtesy card or it's another hour of debate."
Last car peels away. Tent flap reads: "Now serving: No one."

stories.headline: I'm Yielding Mint Manufacturer Doubles Shifts After Gridlock Exodus Drains Urban Stockpiles
stories.deck: Omaha plant cites 300 percent order spike from suburban cul-de-sacs stocked for endless yield rotations
stories.article: The Omaha facility added a third shift after peppermint orders jumped 300 percent, each tin stamped with 1923 traffic statutes still on the books. Warehouse crews installed extra bays for pallets heading to emptied cul-de-sacs. The wrapper slogan 'One at a Time Since Never' continues to move units even without any rule requiring the mints.
